items.title: Codex Desktop "Edit files" shows the Python edit script instead of the actual modified source files

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.924.20706

### What subscription do you have?

plus

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64

### What issue are you seeing?

After updating to the latest Codex version, I noticed that the "Edited files" section at the end of a task no longer correctly shows the source files that were actually modified.

In this task, Codex modified multiple Kotlin source files, including:

- DetectorDataProcessor.kt
- TcpDeviceRepository.kt
- GInterpDataLoader.kt
- AcquisitionViewModel.kt
- ImagingProcessor.kt
- CameraActivity.kt

The task summary also correctly listed these files as the main modified files.

However, the final "Edited files" UI only showed:

- apply_code_comments.py

with:

+377 -0

This Python file appears to be a temporary/helper script created by Codex to perform the code modifications, rather than the actual project files that were changed.

Expected behavior:

The "Edited files" section should show the actual project files whose contents were modified, for example:

- DetectorDataProcessor.kt
- TcpDeviceRepository.kt
- GInterpDataLoader.kt
- AcquisitionViewModel.kt
- ImagingProcessor.kt
- CameraActivity.kt

The implementation method used by Codex (Python script, apply_patch, shell command, etc.) should not affect which files are displayed in the final edited-files summary.

Actual behavior:

Only the helper Python script used to perform the edits is shown in the "Edited files" section, while the real modified source files are missing.

This makes it difficult to review the changes and may also make the Undo / Review UI misleading, because the displayed file is not the actual project file that was modified.

The source files were successfully modified and the project compiled successfully, so the issue appears to be related to file-change tracking or UI attribution rather than the edit operation itself.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Steps to reproduce:

1. Open a project in Codex.
2. Ask Codex to modify several existing source files.
3. Codex creates and runs a Python helper script to perform the modifications.
4. Wait for the task to complete.
5. Check the "Edited files" section at the bottom of the task result.

Result:
Only the Python helper script is shown.

Expected:
All source files whose contents were actually changed should be shown.

### What is the expected behavior?

_No response_

items.body:
## Summary

Immediately after updating the Codex desktop app, the app automatically restarted and macOS displayed a **Malware Blocked** warning for the `codex` executable:

> “codex” was not opened because it contains malware. This action did not harm your Mac.

The warning appeared as part of the first automatic restart after the update.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Codex desktop app on macOS.
2. Install the available app update.
3. Allow the app to restart automatically after the update.
4. Observe the macOS **Malware Blocked** dialog for `codex` immediately after restart.

## Actual behavior

macOS blocks a component named `codex` as malware immediately after the updated app restarts. The Codex UI remains visible behind the warning, but at least one `codex` component is not allowed to launch.

## Expected behavior

The updated app and all bundled executables/helpers should be correctly signed and notarized, and Codex should restart without any Gatekeeper/XProtect malware warning.

## Environment

- Codex/ChatGPT desktop version: **26.924.22138**
- Release date shown in About dialog: **Sep 26, 2026**
- macOS: **Golden Gate 27.0**
- Device: **16-inch MacBook Pro**
- Chip: **Apple M5 Max**
- Memory: **128 GB**

## Additional information

The warning appeared specifically after the updater completed and the app restarted itself. Screenshots of the warning and version information are available. Device serial number and unrelated project/account information have been omitted for privacy.

items.title: [Windows][Desktop][Auth] App hangs on infinite spinner when auth.json exists before process startup

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary

The Codex/ChatGPT Windows desktop app enters an indefinite loading state when a valid $CODEX_HOME\auth.json is already present when the packaged app process starts. The window opens and displays a spinner, but the main application routes never mount.

If auth.json is temporarily moved out of $CODEX_HOME before launching the same app build with the same project database and configuration, the renderer mounts normally. The desktop app later recreates auth.json from the existing account/session, signs in successfully, and loads the project.

This is consistently reproducible with both zero projects and one project in the local project database. The project database does not appear to be the trigger.

## User report and troubleshooting-session context

I am troubleshooting the Codex desktop app on Windows 11 64-bit. For approximately the last month, the app has shown progressively worse performance when sending prompts, including long delays, indefinite buffering, and prompts that appear never to complete. The current failure escalated into an infinite loading spinner during application startup, making the desktop app effectively unusable.

The app was too slow and unresponsive to troubleshoot from within its own interface, so I had to continue the investigation through Codex CLI. This report summarizes that troubleshooting session, the controlled tests performed, the logs collected, and the only reliable workaround found.

## Troubleshooting-session chronology

1. The desktop app reported a database-related problem and offered a retry action.
2. Selecting retry led to a permanent loading spinner.
3. Restarting the app did not clear the spinner.
4. The Microsoft Store app was uninstalled and reinstalled, but the startup failure continued.
5. Local chat/application state was reset while preserving the actual project source directories.
6. Nonessential plugins were removed or disabled to rule out plugin startup failures.
7. Fresh CODEX_HOME profiles were tested with zero and one local project records.
8. The issue reproduced whenever a valid auth.json existed before process startup.
9. Moving only auth.json out of the way before launch allowed the renderer to mount, after which the app recreated authentication and signed in successfully.
10. The original project directory remained untouched and could be added back to the app.

## Impact / severity

High — startup-blocking. The app becomes unusable and local projects/chats cannot be accessed through the normal launcher. Reinstalling and resetting local app data did not resolve it.

## Environment

- OS: Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit
- OS version: 10.0.26200 (build 26200.9457, 25H2)
- Microsoft Store package: OpenAI.Codex_26.924.1866.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0
- Package version: 26.924.1866.0
- Runtime/app version shown in logs: 26.924.20706
- Desktop build number: 11431
- Build commit: 97cf4a3c7cee97ad6cbb13cb9ab228321db3a385
- Bundled app-server version: 0.158.0-alpha.2
- Separately installed Codex CLI: codex-cli 0.154.0
- Authentication method: ChatGPT account login
- Reproduced using clean alternate CODEX_HOME profiles
- Third-party MCP/plugin configuration was removed or disabled during isolation

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set CODEX_HOME to a clean test profile.
2. Authenticate so that $CODEX_HOME\auth.json exists.
3. Fully terminate all Codex/ChatGPT desktop processes.
4. Launch the packaged app using: shell:AppsFolder\OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0!App
5. Observe that the desktop window opens but remains on the loading spinner indefinitely.
6. Fully terminate the app again.
7. Move only $CODEX_HOME\auth.json to a timestamped backup. Do not modify the project database or project files.
8. Launch the exact same packaged app again.
9. Observe that renderer routes mount in approximately 3.5 seconds.
10. Wait for the app to restore/recreate authentication. It signs in and completes startup successfully, with the existing project still present.

## Expected result

The app should read the existing valid authentication state, mount its routes, and show the authenticated home/project UI. An auth refresh failure should produce a recoverable sign-in screen or actionable error rather than block route mounting.

## Actual result

When auth.json exists at process startup, the app window remains on an infinite spinner. In failing runs, logging reaches an authenticated bootstrap/pubsub state but never records app routes mounted or a successful app_start span.

## Reproduction matrix

| Test | auth.json at process start | Local project count | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Clean profile, authenticated | Present | 0 | Infinite spinner |
| Clean profile, authenticated | Present | 1 | Infinite spinner |
| Same profile/database | Temporarily absent | 1 | Routes mount; auth is recreated; startup succeeds |

This matrix rules out the project row as the primary trigger. The differentiating condition is whether auth.json exists before process startup.

## Relevant logs

Failure, zero projects:

    2026-09-26T06:20:38.102Z Local app-server project migration completed projectCount=0
    2026-09-26T06:20:40.308Z response_routed method=account/read
    2026-09-26T06:20:41.373Z codex-home request hostId=undefined
    2026-09-26T06:20:44.260Z chatgpt_pubsub_topic_subscribed topicId=resource-updates

Failure, one project:

    2026-09-26T06:19:15.934Z Local app-server project migration completed projectCount=1
    2026-09-26T06:19:17.892Z response_routed method=account/read
    2026-09-26T06:19:18.929Z codex-home request hostId=undefined
    2026-09-26T06:19:21.723Z chatgpt_pubsub_topic_subscribed topicId=resource-updates

Successful control, auth absent only during launch:

    2026-09-26T06:28:11.191Z Local app-server project migration completed projectCount=1
    2026-09-26T06:28:14.494Z [startup][renderer] app routes mounted after 3546ms
    2026-09-26T06:29:11.085Z [startup][renderer] app routes mounted after 60212ms
    2026-09-26T06:29:11.509Z response_routed method=model/list
    2026-09-26T06:29:11.882Z chatgpt_pubsub_topic_subscribed topicId=resource-updates
    2026-09-26T06:29:11.982Z name=app_start outcome=success buildNumber=11431
    2026-09-26T06:29:12.721Z codex-home request hostId=local

## Troubleshooting already performed

- Fully terminated and restarted the app repeatedly.
- Used the retry flow; it returned to an indefinite spinner.
- Uninstalled and reinstalled the Microsoft Store package.
- Reset the AppX package/local application data.
- Tested multiple fresh CODEX_HOME profiles.
- Tested with zero projects and one project.
- Reauthenticated using Codex CLI.
- Removed/disabled nonessential plugin and MCP configuration.
- Preserved the project directory without modifying source files.
- Confirmed Codex CLI reports a valid ChatGPT login.
- Confirmed that moving only auth.json before startup changes the outcome from failure to success.

## Working workaround

Move auth.json to a timestamped backup immediately before launching the packaged app:

    $codexHome = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.codex-recovery-v4'
    $authPath = Join-Path $codexHome 'auth.json'

    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $authPath) {
        $timestamp = Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd-HHmmss'
        Move-Item -LiteralPath $authPath -Destination (Join-Path $codexHome "auth.preboot-$timestamp.json")
    }

    $env:CODEX_HOME = $codexHome
    Start-Process 'explorer.exe' 'shell:AppsFolder\OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0!App'

The app later recreates auth.json and signs in from the existing desktop account/session. Project data remains intact because the workaround does not remove the project database or project directory.

## Suspected failure area

This is an inference from the A/B startup tests and logs, not a confirmed code-level diagnosis. The renderer appears to wait indefinitely during authenticated bootstrap after account/read, an unresolved codex-home request hostId=undefined, and the resource-update pubsub subscription.

Potential areas to inspect:

- Authenticated renderer bootstrap ordering/race conditions.
- A promise or state transition waiting on codex-home host resolution.
- Pubsub initialization occurring before route mounting without a timeout/error boundary.
- Rehydration of an existing ChatGPT desktop account into the Codex app-server session.
- A missing fallback from authenticated bootstrap to a recoverable sign-in state.

## Requested engineering improvements

1. Prevent auth refresh/bootstrap from indefinitely blocking the renderer's main routes.
2. Add a timeout and visible recovery action around authenticated startup dependencies.
3. Add structured logging after codex-home hostId=undefined.
4. Add a Windows regression test covering the reproduction matrix.
5. Preserve local projects and sessions when authentication recovery is required.

## Security and privacy

Do not request auth.json; it contains authentication credentials/tokens. Account email addresses, account IDs, access tokens, refresh tokens, private project source, and proprietary chat/session contents have been omitted.

Report date: 2026-09-25 America/Los_Angeles; log timestamps are UTC on 2026-09-26.

[Codex-Windows-Auth-Startup-Infinite-Spinner-Bug-Report.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32678782/Codex-Windows-Auth-Startup-Infinite-Spinner-Bug-Report.md)

items.title: [macOS][Browser Use] vk.ru/groups denied by site-safety despite Always allow in built-in browser

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Environment
- ChatGPT desktop app on macOS 15.5, app version 26.924.20706.
- Codex task using the built-in browser (IAB), not the Chrome extension.
- The owner is signed in to their own VK account and manually opened `https://vk.ru/groups`.
- In Settings > Browser, the owner explicitly set `https://vk.ru` → Browsing / View web pages: **Always allow**.

## Problem
Browser Use refuses even read-only attachment to the already-open `https://vk.ru/groups` tab before it can inspect the page. No website-permission prompt or Auto-review is attempted. This prevents the owner-authorized audit of video publications in their own communities.

Exact tool response after the **Always allow** setting was applied:
```text
Browser Use rejected this action due to browser security policy. Reason: The site-safety policy blocks this action; no user permission prompt or Auto-review was attempted. Browser use is not permitted on https://vk.ru/groups. The agent must not attempt to achieve the same outcome via workaround, indirect execution, raw CDP or browser commands, alternate browser surfaces, or policy circumvention. Proceed only with a materially safer alternative that does not require this blocked browser action; if none exists, stop and request user input.
```

## Reproduction
1. Open `https://vk.ru/groups` manually in the desktop app's built-in browser while signed in.
2. Set `https://vk.ru` to **Always allow** for page viewing in Settings > Browser.
3. Ask Codex to select the open IAB tab for a read-only audit.
4. Browser Use rejects `getTab({url:'https://vk.ru/groups'}, {browser:'iab'})` with the response above.

Earlier in the task the agent mistakenly selected an `id.vk.ru/account` tab and received a similar site-safety denial. The owner then explicitly selected `vk.ru/groups` and configured **Always allow**. The direct retry on that correct tab still failed at the site-safety layer. The owner also tried `/approve`, but the final refusal occurred before Auto-review.

## Expected behavior
If read-only VK community inspection is supported, allow it under the explicit site permission or present a recoverable owner approval. If VK is intentionally restricted, please distinguish that restriction from the user-configurable **Always allow** setting and provide an official review/remediation path. We are requesting a supported resolution, not a bypass.

No credentials, cookies, private account identifiers, screenshots, or chat transcript are included. No alternate browser, raw CDP, or indirect VK readback was used after the denial.

Related: #48186 reports a similar `vk.ru/[group]` site-safety error on Windows, with a different environment and a broader diagnostic issue.

## Follow-up after owner reconfirmed access
On the same day, the owner stated that the browser was now permitting VK and explicitly authorized another read-only attempt. The agent tried the same IAB `getTab({url:'https://vk.ru/groups'}, {browser:'iab'})` once. This time the automatic review rejected it as a prohibited retry of the earlier site-safety denial, explicitly noting the owner's authorization. No page state was returned. No alternate browser or indirect access was attempted. The owner then explicitly authorized continued work again; we did not repeat the rejected action. This shows the browser's **Always allow** permission and owner approval still do not provide a supported path to recover from the site-safety refusal.

## Possible trigger reported by owner
The owner reports a temporary loss of connection to their server around the first denial; their Windows browser had successfully inspected VK shortly before. They believe the initial site-safety result may be stale state caused by that outage. We have not verified causality. Please check whether a transient browser/session/backend failure can leave a stale denial attached to the task and whether there is a supported recovery/reset path. The agent did not retry through another browser after the denial.

## Local diagnostic check (26 Sep)
A narrow search of desktop logs found the built-in browser sidebar `dom-ready` for `https://vk.ru/groups` at 07:04:22 UTC. The same minute, the app logged a reconnect attempt to a separate remote worker host. This supports that the owner-opened VK page rendered in the local app while the remote connection was unstable; it does **not** establish that the reconnect caused the site-safety denial. The available task transcript contains only the generic site-safety rejection and no rule/category or classifier trace. Please correlate the attached session ID with internal Browser Use policy decisions to distinguish an intentional block, misclassification, and stale session state.

items.title: Memories: archived threads are never picked up by stage-1, so archiving a finished task drops it from memory

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
## What happens

Archiving a thread permanently removes it from the memories pipeline, even when the thread is still waiting for stage-1 extraction.

Stage-1 selection (`claim_stage1_jobs_for_startup` in `codex-rs/state/src/runtime/memories.rs`) calls `push_thread_filters` with `archived_only: false`. That filter keeps only active threads (`archived = 0`). A thread also has to be idle for `min_rollout_idle_hours` (default 6) before it qualifies. So if I finish a task and archive it right away, which is the normal way to tidy the sidebar, it never becomes eligible. The work in it is never turned into a memory.

The same applies to later turns in a thread that already has a stage-1 output. If new turns arrive (for example heartbeat or automation runs, or more work) and I archive the thread before the idle window ends, the existing output keeps its old `source_updated_at`. The newer turns are never summarized.

Consolidation already handles archived threads correctly: phase-2 selection reads `stage1_outputs` without an archived filter, so memories created before archiving stay available. The problem is limited to stage-1 eligibility.

## Evidence from a real CODEX_HOME (macOS desktop, codex-cli 0.154.0)

- 6,432 archived threads. 284 of them have stage-1 outputs, all created before archiving, and 221 of those are still selected for phase 2.
- Only 1 of the 284 got a stage-1 output after being archived.
- 67 threads archived and updated in the last 7 days have no stage-1 output at all.
- Concrete case: a thread with a stage-1 output at `source_updated_at` 2026-09-24 kept receiving turns until 2026-09-26. Archiving it now would drop those two days from memory for good.

## Why it matters

Archiving is how people keep the task list manageable. Right now it silently decides which work Codex remembers, and it usually drops the most recent and most finished work. Memory quality ends up depending on sidebar habits the user cannot see.

## Proposed behavior

1. Keep archived threads eligible for stage 1 while they are inside `max_rollout_age_days` and `memory_mode = 'enabled'`. Resolve the rollout path from `archived_sessions/`.
2. Optionally, treat archiving as a strong signal that the thread is finished: skip the idle-hours wait and queue stage 1 for the thread soon after it is archived.
3. If excluding archived threads is intentional, document it and make it configurable, for example `[memories] include_archived_threads = true`.

Related: #27121 (manual memory refresh) and #17490 (other stage-1 eligibility gap).

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Installed Windows desktop app: 26.924.20706 (build 11431, production channel). The version was obtained from the app's update check, not the About dialog.

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided.

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64.

### What issue are you seeing?

After an app update on 2026-09-26 (Asia/Shanghai), the user reports that references to selected response annotations no longer display or load correctly across assistant replies in an existing conversation. In one captured, redacted reply, the internal reference appeared visibly as literal text:

~~~text
`:codex-annotation{index="1"}`
~~~

The backticks in that captured assistant reply put the directive in Markdown inline code. That can explain this particular occurrence by itself. It is not yet established whether the other reported failures have the same generated formatting, a desktop rendering problem, or missing annotation data. Please investigate the generation/rendering boundary rather than assuming a single client-side root cause.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

These are privacy-safe steps based on the affected workflow. The synthetic wording below has not been independently tested in a fresh conversation.

1. In the Windows Codex desktop app, open an existing conversation and ask for a short reply such as "Alpha beta gamma."
2. Select "beta" in that assistant reply, choose **Add to chat**, attach a comment such as "Please explain this selection," and send it.
3. Inspect the assistant's next reply where it refers to the selected response annotation.
4. In the affected conversation, the reference is displayed as raw directive text or cannot be opened as an annotation reference. One captured reply rendered the directive as inline code, as shown above.

### What is the expected behavior?

The reply should display a usable reference to the selected passage. Activating it should resolve the original annotation instead of exposing internal directive syntax.

### Additional information

- Reported after updating on 2026-09-26 local time; the first affected build is unknown.
- This report intentionally includes no original conversation text, user comment, thread/session ID, repository path, screenshot, or logs. The reproduction phrases are synthetic.
- Related but different reports: #35426 concerns raw Markdown leaking into selected annotation content; #43951 concerns the response-selection control disappearing mid-session.

Four previously working local, project-scoped cron automations stopped producing scheduled runs. They remain `ACTIVE`, but the persisted `next_run_at` values are now in the past and have not advanced. This affects two independent projects and both daily and weekly schedules.

Read-only diagnostics on 2026-09-26 found the following in `$CODEX_HOME/sqlite/codex-dev.db`. Task names are anonymized; all timestamps below are UTC:

| Task | Intended schedule (Europe/Moscow) | last_run_at | next_run_at (stale) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Project A, weekly task 1 | Wednesday 20:00 | 2026-09-09 20:52:31.885Z | 2026-09-16 20:00:10Z |
| Project A, weekly task 2 | Sunday 11:00 | 2026-09-09 20:52:31.836Z | 2026-09-13 11:01:37Z |
| Project B, daily task 1 | 09:00 and 21:00 | 2026-09-11 15:35:03.296Z | 2026-09-11 18:00:28Z |
| Project B, daily task 2 | 15:00 | 2026-09-11 15:35:03.320Z | 2026-09-12 12:00:12Z |

The newest row in the local `automation_runs` table is dated `2026-09-11T15:35:04.284Z`. The four automation TOML files also still say `status = "ACTIVE"` and `execution_environment = "local"`.

The desktop app was running during the investigation. Its September 26 logs contain normal app-server activity, including repeated `configRequirements/read` responses around the morning scheduling window, but no automation/scheduler/cron entries were found in that day's logs. This does not establish that the machine was awake for every earlier missed occurrence.

The local database is diagnostic evidence, not proof that this version still uses it as its authoritative scheduler state. If these records became legacy after a migration, please investigate why the previously configured tasks no longer execute or expose a clear migration/error status.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence (not yet reproduced on a clean profile):

1. Create local project automations with daily and weekly schedules and run them successfully over multiple days.
2. Continue using the desktop app. In this profile, recorded automation runs stop after September 11 even though the tasks remain active.
3. On September 26, inspect the saved task configurations and local scheduling/run records read-only.
4. Observe overdue `next_run_at` values, no newer run records, and no new scheduled execution results.

Representative recurrence rules:

```text
FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9,21;BYMINUTE=0;BYSECOND=0
FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=15;BYMINUTE=0;BYSECOND=0

DTSTART;TZID=Europe/Moscow:20260902T200000
RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=WE;BYHOUR=20;BYMINUTE=0
```

A read-only query used for verification:

```sql
SELECT id, status, last_run_at, next_run_at FROM automations;
SELECT MAX(created_at) AS latest_run FROM automation_runs;
```

No direct writes to the scheduler database were made. A full desktop restart has been proposed but has not been confirmed or tested as a recovery in this investigation.

### What is the expected behavior?

Active recurring tasks should execute at future scheduled times when the app, machine, and project are available. If execution is disabled by migration, account eligibility, a scheduler failure, or another prerequisite, the app should expose an actionable error instead of leaving apparently active tasks with stale scheduling state.

### Additional information

- The active agent session no longer exposes an automation-management tool, so the agent could not repair/resave the tasks through that interface. Related report: #30905. This is a secondary symptom, not an established cause of missed runs.
- #17893 describes heartbeat tasks whose `next_run_at` **advances** without execution. Here, previously working **cron** tasks have `next_run_at` **stuck in the past**, across multiple schedules.
- The weekly UTC timestamps also appear offset from the intended Moscow wall-clock time; #26633 may be relevant, but that alone does not explain the daily tasks stopping too.
- A separate one-shot task with `COUNT=1` was excluded from the four affected recurring tasks; its absent next execution is expected.
- Individual task-level failures do exist, but those are distinct from the absence of newly recorded scheduled runs. No causal link to the scheduler stall has been established.
- Tokens, account identifiers, local usernames/paths, task prompts, financial records, and full application logs are intentionally omitted.

Please investigate scheduler activation/task migration and provide a supported recovery path that preserves existing tasks and avoids duplicate execution of overdue work.

items.title: app-server: SIGTERM between socket publication and signal-handler setup leaves the unix:// alias, socket and lock behind

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What version of Codex is running?

codex-cli 0.157.1 (same code on `main` and `rust-v0.157.0`)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.8.0-138-generic x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`run_main_with_transport_options` starts the Unix control socket acceptor
(`codex-rs/app-server/src/lib.rs:783`), which binds the socket and publishes the `--listen` path as a symlink
(`app-server-transport/src/transport/unix_socket.rs:98-110`). The SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP handler
(`shutdown_signal()`) is first armed later, at `lib.rs:1027`. A SIGTERM delivered in between takes the default
action, so no destructor runs.

```sh
export HOME=$(mktemp -d) CODEX_HOME=$HOME/.codex; mkdir -p "$CODEX_HOME"
run=$(mktemp -d); chmod 700 "$run"
codex app-server --listen "unix://$run/b.sock" & pid=$!
while [ ! -L "$run/b.sock" ]; do :; done
kill -TERM $pid; wait $pid; echo "exit=$?"      # exit=143
ls -la "$run/b.sock"; ls -la "/tmp/codex-daemon-$(id -u)/"
```

### What is the expected behavior?

A supervisor that sees the published path and then stops the server with SIGTERM (systemd, a process manager,
a test harness) gets a clean shutdown: the alias, the socket and the lock are removed, as they are for a SIGINT
after startup completes.

### What do you see instead?

The process dies with 143 and leaves the `b.sock` alias, the socket it points to, and the `.lock` file. Until a
server is started again on the same path (which does clean up its own stale alias in
`prepare_control_socket_path`), clients find a published path whose socket refuses connections; for a path
that is never reused, the files stay forever.

### Additional information

Arming the signal handler (or installing the SIGTERM listener) before `start_control_socket_acceptor` publishes
the path would close the window; the published alias is the signal to supervisors that the server is up.

items.title: app-server: --listen unix:// leaves a <hash>.lock in /tmp/codex-daemon-<uid> for every socket path, never removed

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What version of Codex is running?

codex-cli 0.157.1 (same code on `main` and `rust-v0.157.0`)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.8.0-138-generic x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Since 0.156.0, `codex app-server --listen unix://PATH` binds its socket at
`<realpath /tmp>/codex-daemon-<euid>/<sha256 of canonical PATH>` and publishes `PATH` as a symlink to it.
Before binding it takes a startup lock on `<same hash>.lock` in that directory
(`acquire_app_server_startup_lock`, `codex-rs/app-server-transport/src/transport/unix_socket.rs:76-79`).

```sh
export HOME=$(mktemp -d) CODEX_HOME=$HOME/.codex; mkdir -p "$CODEX_HOME"
run=$(mktemp -d); chmod 700 "$run"
codex app-server --listen "unix://$run/a.sock" & pid=$!
sleep 3; hash=$(basename "$(readlink "$run/a.sock")")
kill -INT $pid; wait $pid            # exit 0, clean shutdown
ls -la "/tmp/codex-daemon-$(id -u)/$hash" "/tmp/codex-daemon-$(id -u)/$hash.lock"
```

### What is the expected behavior?

After a clean shutdown nothing that belongs to that listener remains in `/tmp/codex-daemon-<euid>`.

### What do you see instead?

The socket and the `PATH` alias are removed (`ControlSocketFileGuard::drop`, `unix_socket.rs:348-365`), but the
zero-byte `<hash>.lock` stays. Nothing ever removes it, so the directory gains one file per distinct socket path
ever served. Every caller that uses per-session or temporary socket paths (tests, supervisors, one socket per
workspace) grows it without bound; on one workstation it held 42 orphaned `.lock` files and one live socket.

### Additional information

Removing a lock file that other processes may still `open()` needs care (the unlink-while-locked race), so a
plain `remove_file` in `Drop` is not enough on its own. Options: unlink the lock while still holding it and have
`acquire_app_server_startup_lock` re-check that the locked file is still the one at the path after `lock()`
(retry if not), or key the lock on the directory rather than on each path.

items.title: Resume picker hides app-created threads with history when preview is empty

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
## Problem

Threads created through the desktop app’s `create_thread` tool can contain substantial conversation history and have a persisted name, but remain absent from `codex resume --all`.

On my machine, 62 non-archived CLI/app threads in one project were excluded. All 62 contained `create_thread` tool output but no user-message event. The 11 visible threads all contained user-message events. The missing threads had the correct project directory, `source = vscode`, and `archived = 0`.

## Cause

The initial task input is recorded as `ItemCompleted(FunctionCallOutput)` for `create_thread`, with a `<codex_delegation>` payload, rather than `ItemCompleted(UserMessage)`.

In `codex-rs/state/src/extract.rs`, `apply_event_msg` populates previews from user messages (including `ItemCompleted(UserMessage)`) and goal objectives, but not this tool output. Consequently, these threads retain an empty `threads.preview`.

In `codex-rs/state/src/runtime/threads.rs`, `push_thread_filters_with_preview` excludes these threads from ordinary active listings:

```sql
AND threads.preview <> ''
```

The resume picker uses that listing. Selecting “All” removes the directory filter, not the empty-preview filter.

One visible thread created through the same tool had subsequently received the user message `continue`; its stored preview is literally `continue`.

## Reproduction

1. Have the desktop app create a named task through `create_thread` and let it perform work.
2. Do not send a regular user message directly to the created thread.
3. Open `codex resume --all`.
4. Observe that the thread is absent even though the desktop app displays its name and conversation history.

The affected local records have an empty `preview` and `first_user_message`, despite containing completed conversation items in their rollout files.

## Expected behavior

A named thread containing initial task input and conversation history should appear in the resume picker without requiring an additional user message.

An empty preview should not, by itself, mean that a thread is empty or disposable.

## Fix pointers

A narrow fix to consider is preserving named threads in the listing:

```sql
AND (threads.preview <> '' OR COALESCE(threads.name, '') <> '')
```

This would expose existing affected threads without rewriting their metadata, while continuing to hide unnamed sessions with empty previews. It would not cover unnamed threads created through `create_thread`, and it would also make explicitly named empty sessions visible.

A broader fix could populate previews from `create_thread` task input, including a backfill for existing threads, or base listing visibility on meaningful history instead of preview presence.

A regression test should cover a named thread with `create_thread` task input, conversation history, and an empty preview, alongside an unnamed empty session that should remain hidden.

## Related

[Forked session is hidden from resume picker until its first new message](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/39553) reports the same listing filter hiding forks. This report supplies a separate trigger: threads created through the desktop app’s `create_thread` tool.

## Environment

- Codex CLI: `0.157.1`
- Platform: macOS
- Affected thread history mode: `paginated`

In ChatGPT/Codex version `26.917.62051` & ‘26.924.20706’, once the OpenAI provider reaches its usage limit, the Send button remains disabled even after switching to a valid third-party provider.

The issue affects both existing tasks and newly created tasks. This indicates that the disabled state is not scoped to a single conversation and is not caused by the third-party provider.

## Environment

- Product: ChatGPT/Codex desktop app
- Version: `26.917.62051`
- Original provider: OpenAI
- Replacement provider: Valid third-party provider
- Date observed: September 24, 2026

## Preconditions

- The OpenAI provider has reached its usage limit.
- The third-party provider API is valid and reachable.
- The third-party provider can successfully handle requests independently.
- The provider switch is accepted by the application.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use the OpenAI provider in the desktop app.
2. Exhaust the available OpenAI usage or reach the provider limit.
3. Observe that the Send button becomes disabled.
4. Switch the provider to a valid third-party provider.
5. Select a compatible model.
6. Open an existing task and attempt to send a message.
7. Create a new task and attempt to send a message.

## Actual behavior

The Send button remains greyed out in both:

- existing tasks;
- newly created tasks.

The behavior persists after switching to a valid third-party provider. The third-party API itself is functional, so the disabled state is not caused by provider availability or API credentials.

## Expected behavior

After switching to a valid provider, the application should recompute the global composer availability state and allow the user to send messages.

Provider-specific usage exhaustion should not disable message composition globally after the active provider has changed.

## Impact

The user cannot continue working through a configured third-party provider after OpenAI usage is exhausted.

Because newly created tasks are also affected, the issue can make the entire desktop app appear unable to send messages until the client state is reset or the usage window recovers.

## Regression context

Previously, after OpenAI usage was exhausted, switching to a valid third-party provider still allowed messages to be sent. The current behavior appears to be a regression in version `26.917.62051`.

## Likely cause

The client may retain a global provider/quota failure state after the OpenAI provider becomes unavailable. The provider switch updates the selected provider but does not clear or recompute one or more global state values, such as:

- `canSend`;
- provider quota exhaustion;
- global request availability;
- composer disabled state;
- cached authentication or capability validation;
- an application-level error state.

Because both old and new tasks are affected, this state is likely held above the task/conversation level.

## Suggested fix

When the active provider, model, endpoint, or credential context changes:

1. Clear provider-specific quota and error state.
2. Recompute global composer availability.
3. Revalidate the selected provider and model.
4. Cancel or invalidate pending requests associated with the previous provider.
5. Enable the Send button when the new provider is valid.
6. If the new provider cannot be used for the current task, show a specific error instead of leaving the Send button silently disabled.

## Suggested regression test

```text
OpenAI provider reaches usage limit
→ Send button becomes disabled
→ switch to a valid third-party provider
→ select a compatible model
→ create a new task
→ Send button becomes enabled
→ message is submitted successfully
```

The test should also verify that an existing task and a newly created task behave consistently.

## Additional evidence available

- Desktop app version: `26.917.62051`
- Existing and newly created tasks are both affected
- Third-party provider API is independently verified as valid
- The issue is reproducible after OpenAI usage is exhausted

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start Codex desktop version `26.917.62051`.
2. Create or open a task using the OpenAI provider.
3. Consume the available OpenAI usage until the provider reaches its usage limit.
4. Confirm that the Send button becomes disabled/greyed out.
5. Switch the configured provider to a valid third-party provider with a working API key and endpoint.
6. Select a compatible model from that provider.
7. Try to send a short message in the existing task.
8. Create a new task and try to send the same message again.

The bug reproduces in both existing and newly created tasks. The Send button remains disabled after switching providers, even though the third-party API is independently verified to be valid and reachable.

This suggests that provider quota exhaustion leaves a global disabled state in the client. The state is not cleared or recomputed when the active provider changes.

A minimal configuration example is:

```toml
# Before: OpenAI provider reaches its usage limit
model_provider = "openai"
model = "<openai-model>"

# After switching: valid third-party provider
model_provider = "third-party"
model = "<third-party-model>"
base_url = "https://api.example.com/v1"
api_key = "<valid-api-key>"
```

The expected behavior is that the Send button becomes enabled immediately after the valid provider and model are selected, or after starting a new task.

The following information should be attached to the report rather than fabricated:

```text
Session ID: <session-id, if available>
Codex version: 26.917.62051
OpenAI token limit usage: <value shown by the client, if available>
Context window usage: <value shown by the client, if available>
Third-party provider: <provider name>
Third-party model: <model ID>
Operating system: <OS and version>
```

No code snippet is required to trigger the defect because it is a client-side UI state issue; the configuration above represents the provider transition that triggers it.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.157.1

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro (5x)

### Which model were you using?

gpt-6-astra

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.2.6-1-cachyos x86_64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

foot 1.28.0 on Hyprland, no multiplexer

### Codex doctor report

```json
not available, didn't run it
```

### What issue are you seeing?

After logging in with `codex login` from a normal shell, running `codex` still puts me on the sign in screen. Logging in again just loops back to the same screen. It only goes away after `codex app-server daemon restart`.

I ran into this because of #48363 (the TUI wouldn't open the browser so I used `codex login` instead).

From what I can tell, `account/read` answers from `auth_manager.auth_cached()`, and the daemon only calls `reload()` after a login it ran itself (the ChatGPT login completion, API key login, Bedrock login). If another process writes auth.json, like `codex login` or `codex logout`, the long running daemon never notices, so the TUI keeps thinking you're logged out.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Clean CODEX_HOME, 0.157.1:

1. `codex app-server daemon start` while logged out
2. `codex`, it shows the sign in screen (expected), quit
3. `printenv OPENAI_API_KEY | codex login --with-api-key` (plain `codex login` does the same thing)
4. `codex` again, still shows the sign in screen
5. `codex app-server daemon restart`, then `codex`, now it's logged in

### What is the expected behavior?

The daemon picks up a login or logout saved by another process without needing a restart.

### Additional information

Fix on my fork: https://github.com/Kuenec/codex/commit/6ad67f8e739ef3dc11236a8dad87915f53aabebd

It reloads stored auth at the start of `account/read` and rebinds the cloud config loader when it changed, the same way it does after a login. It skips the reload when external auth is active (host tokens or workload identity) since that goes through the provider instead of storage. There's a test in `app-server/tests/suite/v2/account.rs` that fails without it. Other connected clients still won't get an `account/updated` for a change picked up this way, didn't touch that.

- Bundled app-server / CLI runtime: `0.158.0-alpha.2`

### What subscription do you have?

No ChatGPT subscription, and the app is **not signed in to ChatGPT**. Codex Desktop is configured against a third-party provider with an API key (key redacted):

```toml
model_provider = "custom"
[model_providers.custom]
name = "<third-party provider>"
base_url = "https://<provider-host>"
wire_api = "responses"

# experimental_bearer_token = <redacted>
```

`codex doctor` reports `auth  OpenAI auth is not required for the active model provider`, and no `auth.json` exists in `CODEX_HOME`.

### What platform is your computer?

`10.0.19045 x64` (Windows 10 Pro 22H2)

### What issue are you seeing?

Clicking **Archive** on an existing local conversation (sidebar / Recent tasks menu) shows this toast, and the conversation is never archived:

```
Could not determine the account for worktree cleanup.
```

The conversation stays in the active list and never appears in Archived chats. The failure happens before any `thread/archive` request is sent - the desktop log shows the archive intent with no follow-up RPC:

```
info [electron-message-handler] Archive requested conversationId=<ID-A> ... source=recent_tasks_menu
<toast: Could not determine the account for worktree cleanup.>
   <- no `method=thread/archive` for <ID-A>

info [electron-message-handler] Archive requested conversationId=<ID-B> ... source=recent_tasks_menu
info [AppServerConnection] response_routed ... conversationId=<ID-B> ... method=thread/archive ... errorCode=null
   <- the only archive attempt on this build that reached app-server
```

Triggering the same archive action through the app itself (not the UI button) also returns `success=false` with the same message and emits no RPC.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Codex Desktop on Windows with a third-party provider, and not signed in to ChatGPT (`requires_openai_auth = false`, no `auth.json`).
2. Right-click an older local conversation, then Archive.
3. The toast `Could not determine the account for worktree cleanup.` appears; the conversation stays in the active list.

`Archive requested` vs actual `method=thread/archive` emissions in all local desktop logs (deduplicated per log file by conversation id):

| desktop release | date | `Archive requested` | `thread/archive` emitted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 26.908.40834 | 2026-09-12 | 4 | 4 |
| 26.915.31945 | 2026-09-19 | 8 | 8 |
| 26.917.71314 | 2026-09-25 .. 2026-09-26 00:49 | 6 | 6 |
| **26.924.20706** | **2026-09-26** | **13** | **1** |

Failing examples: `<ID-A>` (cwd `D:\<workspace>\here`), `<ID-C>` (cwd `D:\<workspace>\test`). The only success was `<ID-B>` (cwd `D:\<workspace>\nai-prompt-assistant`).

### What is the expected behavior?

Archiving a local conversation from the desktop UI should succeed. When the active provider does not require OpenAI auth, archiving should not depend on a ChatGPT account being resolvable.

### Additional information

This does not look like an auth-state change: the app-server log DB covers 2026-09-18 .. 2026-09-26 and contains no login/logout events, and the `remote control requires ChatGPT authentication` startup warnings appear in bursts both in sessions where archiving worked (2026-09-25 16:16-16:45, 2026-09-26 00:44-00:57) and in the failing session (2026-09-26 13:00+).

**Duplicate check:** searching the exact string `Could not determine the account for worktree cleanup.` (this repository and GitHub issues generally) returns no results, so this appears unreported.

items.title: [Windows] Codex startup intermittently stalls with the desktop pet/avatar overlay enabled

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Pro, version 10.0.26200 (x64)
- Codex Windows app: 26.924.1866.0 (Microsoft Store/MSIX)
- `codex/app-server`: 0.158.0-alpha.2

## Description

On Windows, Codex intermittently remains on a blank/loading screen during startup instead of completing initialization in the primary window. On this machine, enabling the desktop pet/avatar overlay substantially increases the failure rate. Disabling or hiding the overlay reduces the rate but does not eliminate the startup failure.

I am not claiming that the overlay is the sole cause. The results suggest that it is a strong trigger or amplifier for an underlying startup/bootstrap race.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Codex with the desktop pet/avatar overlay enabled (`electron-avatar-overlay-open=true` in the candidate global state).
2. Repeat startup attempts. On the affected machine, the primary window often remains blank/loading.
3. Repeat with the same candidate global state except `electron-avatar-overlay-open=false`, or with the pet/overlay hidden.
4. Compare the outcomes across repeated launches.

## A/B test results

Before every attempt, I restored the exact same candidate global-state file for that test condition. This prevents state changes made by a previous launch from contaminating the next attempt.

| State | Launch failures |
| --- | ---: |
| Original global state, `electron-avatar-overlay-open=true` | 9/9 |
| Clean global state, with only `electron-avatar-overlay-open=true` added | about 10/12 |
| Original global state, changing only the overlay key to `false` | 1/5 |
| Pet/avatar overlay manually hidden | about 20-30% |

The overlay-off runs still failed occasionally, so disabling the overlay is only a workaround and does not fully resolve the startup problem.

## Relevant log observations

- In the representative failed launch, the app-server reports version `0.158.0-alpha.2`, and the primary window reaches `main frame finished load` and `ready-to-show`.
- The avatar-overlay renderer reaches `app routes mounted`. In that failed session, the primary renderer has no corresponding `app routes mounted` or `app_start outcome=success` event before the session ends.
- In the successful comparison, the primary renderer mounts routes and logs `app_start outcome=success`. The `codex-home` request first appears with `hostId=undefined` and later with `hostId=local`.
- These observations show where the two launches diverge; they do not identify the underlying race or prove that the overlay alone causes it.

### Failed launch (2026-09-26 03:36 UTC)

```text
2026-09-26T03:36:41.929Z info [AppServerConnection] Starting app-server connection hostId=local transport=stdio
2026-09-26T03:36:42.121Z info [AppServerConnection] Current reported app-server version: currentVersion=0.158.0-alpha.2 hostId=local
2026-09-26T03:36:42.149Z info [window-manager] window main frame finished load appearance=primary hostId=local startupElapsedMs=213
2026-09-26T03:36:42.182Z info [window-manager] window ready-to-show appearance=primary hostId=local startupElapsedMs=246
2026-09-26T03:36:45.998Z info [electron-fetch-handler] codex-home request hostId=undefined
2026-09-26T03:36:46.143Z info [window-manager] window main frame finished load appearance=avatarOverlay hostId=local startupElapsedMs=227
2026-09-26T03:36:46.147Z info [window-manager] window ready-to-show appearance=avatarOverlay hostId=local startupElapsedMs=231
2026-09-26T03:36:48.745Z info [electron-message-handler] [startup][renderer] app routes mounted after 2806ms rendererWindowAppearance=avatarOverlay rendererWindowVisible=false
```

The complete failed-launch log has no primary-renderer `app routes mounted` or `app_start outcome=success` record.

### Successful launch (2026-09-26 03:10 UTC)

```text
2026-09-26T03:10:09.215Z info [AppServerConnection] Starting app-server connection hostId=local transport=stdio
2026-09-26T03:10:09.376Z info [AppServerConnection] Current reported app-server version: currentVersion=0.158.0-alpha.2 hostId=local
2026-09-26T03:10:09.418Z info [window-manager] window main frame finished load appearance=primary hostId=local startupElapsedMs=198
2026-09-26T03:10:09.455Z info [window-manager] window ready-to-show appearance=primary hostId=local startupElapsedMs=235
2026-09-26T03:10:11.767Z info [electron-fetch-handler] codex-home request hostId=undefined
2026-09-26T03:10:12.211Z info [electron-message-handler] [startup][renderer] app routes mounted after 2963ms rendererWindowAppearance=primary rendererWindowVisible=true
2026-09-26T03:10:17.610Z info [window-manager] window main frame finished load appearance=avatarOverlay hostId=local startupElapsedMs=376
2026-09-26T03:10:17.927Z info [window-manager] window ready-to-show appearance=avatarOverlay hostId=local startupElapsedMs=694
2026-09-26T03:10:30.910Z info [electron-fetch-handler] codex-home request hostId=undefined
2026-09-26T03:10:33.117Z info [electron-message-handler] [startup][renderer] app routes mounted after 23869ms rendererWindowAppearance=primary rendererWindowVisible=true
2026-09-26T03:10:34.672Z info [electron-fetch-handler] codex-home request hostId=local
2026-09-26T03:10:41.227Z info [electron-message-handler] client.performance.span name=app_start outcome=success hostType=electron durationMs=31960.7 wallDurationMs=31959.8
```

The successful log has two primary route-mount events; the app is ultimately recorded as successful after about 32 seconds.

## Workaround

Close or hide the desktop pet/avatar overlay before launching Codex. This reduces the failure rate on my machine but does not eliminate it.

## Related reports

- [#44739](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/44739) reports a Windows pet/avatarOverlay `AppRoutes` crash with `r is not a function`. My failed log does not show that exception; it shows the overlay routes mounting while the primary renderer never records a route mount.
- [#44720](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/44720) documents a related `AppRoutes` startup/pet-window failure on an earlier macOS build. This report adds Windows 11 10.0.26200 on app 26.924.1866.0 and controlled overlay-state A/B results.
- [#36980](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/36980) and [#37073](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/37073) discuss avatar-overlay renderer lifecycle and hidden-overlay event load, respectively; neither documents this startup A/B pattern.

The excerpts above are redacted. They omit local/profile/workspace paths, process and request identifiers, and account metadata. No credentials, account identifiers, thread IDs, conversation contents, or full raw logs are included.

labels.name: bug

labels.name: auth

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.157.1

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro (5x)

### Which model were you using?

gpt-6-astra

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.2.6-1-cachyos x86_64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

foot 1.28.0 on Hyprland, no multiplexer

### Codex doctor report

```json
not available, didn't run it
```

### What issue are you seeing?

Since updating to 0.157.1 the sign in screen in the TUI says "Finish signing in via your browser" but the browser never opens. It just sits there with the link. `codex login` from a normal shell opens the browser fine, and 0.156.1 was fine too.

I looked into it a bit. `maybe_open_auth_url_in_browser` in `tui/src/onboarding/auth.rs` returns early unless the handle is `AppServerRequestHandle::InProcess`. In 0.157 the TUI connects to the managed local daemon over the unix socket by default, so the handle is `Remote` and it never gets to `webbrowser::open`. The app server side starts the login server with `open_browser: false` (`account_processor.rs`), so nothing opens it at all.

To confirm I put logging shims for xdg-settings, xdg-open and my browser first in PATH. `codex login` calls xdg-settings and then the browser like you'd expect. The TUI sign in screen doesn't call any of them.

Skipping the browser makes sense for an actual `--remote` server since the callback lands on that machine's localhost, but the local daemon is on the same machine so it should open like before.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Linux, standalone install on 0.157.1, logged out (`codex logout`)
2. Run `codex` so it picks up the local daemon
3. Choose Sign in with ChatGPT
4. Browser doesn't open, the link only shows in the TUI

### What is the expected behavior?

Browser opens on its own like it does with `codex login` and did in 0.156.1.

### Additional information

Made a small fix on my fork that passes whether the app server target is actually remote into the onboarding auth widget, so it only skips the browser for `AppServerTarget::Remote`: https://github.com/openai/codex/compare/main...Kuenec:codex:tui-login-browser-local-daemon

Built it and tried it against a local daemon and the browser opens again. I know you don't take PRs so just leaving it here in case it helps.

6. Downgrade ChatGPT Desktop to `26.917.71314-1` without changing any other system, network, or account settings.
7. Launch ChatGPT Desktop again and open the same conversation.
8. The conversation loads normally after the downgrade.

### What is the expected behavior?

Existing conversations should load normally when opened from the conversation history, just as they do in the ChatGPT web app and mobile app.

### Additional information

Environment:

- Fedora Workstation 44
- x86_64
- GNOME
- Wayland
- ChatGPT Desktop package: official OpenAI RPM

Regression test:

- `26.924.20706-1` → existing conversations remain stuck loading
- `26.917.71314-1` → the same conversations load normally

No account, network, Fedora, Wayland, or ChatGPT profile settings were changed between the two tests.

The same account and conversations also work normally in the ChatGPT web app and mobile app.

items.body:
## 问题概述

Windows Codex 桌面端的内置浏览器可由用户手动打开普通网页，但 Browser Use 间歇性或持续无法读取页面。浏览器列表/标签列表有时可返回；取得标签、读取页面可访问性状态或创建标签后的状态读取会在约 15–30 秒超时。桌面日志在同一请求期间反复报告 `No ChatGPT browser route is available for browser session <已脱敏>`。

该故障在公开页面 `https://example.com/` 上复现，因此并非某个业务网站特有。

## 环境

- Windows x64，系统版本 10.0.26100
- Codex 桌面端日志中的应用版本：`26.917.71314`
- Windows 应用包路径显示版本：`26.917.9434.0`
- Windows 原生运行；已确认 WSL mixed runtime = FALSE
- 内置浏览器（IAB）；`cua_node` runtime、`node_repl` binary 与 MCP startup 均通过基础检查

## 最小复现

1. 在 Codex 桌面端打开内置浏览器，导航至 `https://example.com/`。
2. 请求 Codex 仅读取当前页面标题，或调用 `cua.getTab({ url: "https://example.com/" }, { browser: "iab" })`。
3. 请求在约 15–30 秒后超时，出现 `js execution timed out; kernel reset, rerun your request`；有时状态为 `apps=[]`、`browsers=[]`、`nodeRepl.fetch request failed`。
4. 在部分重启后的会话中，`cua.listTabs({ browser: "iab" })` 可以迅速列出 `Example Domain` 标签，但取得该标签以读取页面内容仍超时。创建测试标签的调用也曾超时，但之后的标签列表显示它实际已创建。
5. 同期应用日志继续出现浏览器路由错误。

## 已完成的最小 A/B

- `example.com` 曾成功读取一次，之后在同一类操作中再次失败：间歇性。
- 业务网站和 `example.com` 都曾失败：非站点特定。
- 切换到另一个美国 VPN 节点后，同一 `example.com` 读取仍失败。
- 保持该节点并完整重启 Codex 后，标签发现部分恢复，但页面内容读取仍失败。
- 新建 Codex 任务也未解决（用户此前已测试）。
- 内置浏览器由用户手动加载网页通常正常。
- `codex doctor` 曾报告 WebSocket 和部分 HTTP Provider 不可达；桌面日志也曾记录 `net::ERR_PROXY_CONNECTION_FAILED`。这些说明网络/代理可能参与触发，但换节点和重启后持续存在的路由错误不能单独归因为 VPN。

## 脱敏日志摘录

以下仅保留错误类型和已观察到的时间；会话 ID、账号、URL 参数及本地路径均未附上：

```text
2026-09-23 22:07:04 CST  net::ERR_PROXY_CONNECTION_FAILED
2026-09-23 22:09:36 CST  [browser-use-iab-api] IAB_LIFECYCLE iab backend info request failed
                           No ChatGPT browser route is available for browser session <redacted>
2026-09-26 12:47:45 CST  No ChatGPT browser route is available for browser session <redacted>
2026-09-26 12:55:50 CST  No ChatGPT browser route is available for browser session <redacted>
```

## 预期与实际

预期：内置浏览器已打开 `example.com` 时，Browser Use 能取得该标签并读取标题/页面状态；若路由失效，应返回可操作的组件错误，不应长时间超时或产生实际已创建但调用失败的隐藏测试标签。

实际：用户能看到网页；自动化控制时常超时。标签发现与标签内容读取的结果可能不一致。

## 请求调查

请检查 Windows 桌面端 IAB route 注册、会话 ID 绑定、tab RPC/readiness 和超时后的清理逻辑，并说明是否存在受支持的会话恢复方法。特别希望区分代理/WebSocket 中断与 Electron/native pipe 会话绑定丢失。当前用户没有执行重装、删除 `.codex`、删除 runtime 或清空全部缓存。

相关公开报告：#45028、#47123、#44364。

## 应用内反馈

用户已通过当前 Codex 对话中的 `/feedback` 提交会话与日志。反馈 ID：`01a0ce96-8515-73d2-9034-089b68e547ce`。请将该私有诊断包与此 issue 关联；原始日志未公开上传。

items.title: thread/list: omitted modelProviders filters to the server default provider, hiding other threads

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: custom-model
labels.description: Issues related to custom model providers (including local models)

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
## Problem

Codex app-server's `thread/list` treats an omitted `modelProviders` parameter as "filter to the server's configured default provider" rather than "all threads".

Observed on `codex app-server` 0.155.0-alpha.16 / 0.158.0-alpha.2 (Windows), driven over the WebSocket JSON-RPC API:

- Config: `model_provider = "custom"` + a `[model_providers.custom]` table
- Threads created earlier under the built-in `openai` provider (~5,200 rows)
- `thread/list` **without** `modelProviders` → returns only the threads tagged `custom` (1 item)
- `thread/list` with `modelProviders: []` → returns all threads

So omission and an explicit empty list behave differently, and omission silently hides most of the user's history.

## Impact

Clients that omit `modelProviders` — notably the ChatGPT mobile remote-control client — render an almost-empty thread list on any host whose default provider differs from the provider its existing threads were created with. Nothing in the host's data is lost; the threads are simply filtered out of the default view.

## Suggestion

Either:

- treat omitted `modelProviders` as "no provider filter" (same as `[]`), or
- document the default-provider semantics and have remote-control clients send the full configured provider list explicitly.

Repro steps: configure a second provider, set it as `model_provider`, keep older `openai`-tagged threads, then compare `thread/list` with and without `modelProviders`.

items.body:
# 问题摘要

Windows 上的 Codex CLI 0.157.1 在共享 daemon 模式中，发送一条纯文字消息也会短暂弹出多个 Windows Terminal 窗口。捕获到发送阶段的四条自动 Git 查询，以及回复结束时的 Computer Use 通知程序；该轮助手没有调用工具。新建 `--no-daemon` 对话的单轮纯文字对照没有弹窗。

关联 #44768（共享 daemon 启动 hooks／命令时弹窗）和 #33254（Computer Use 结束通知闪窗）。本报告补充的场景是：**发送普通消息、没有助手工具调用时，daemon 自动执行的 Git 查询也伴随可见终端窗口**。这可能与 #44768 共用根因，请按需要合并跟踪；本机尚未证明精确源码根因。

## 环境

- Codex CLI：`0.157.1`，通过 npm 安装。
- 操作系统：Windows 11 x64。
- 使用终端：Warp，PowerShell 7；Warp 精确版本本次未记录。
- 闪出窗口所属程序：Windows Terminal `1.24.11911.0`。
- 模型：`gpt-6-astra`。
- 实际处理会话的进程：`%USERPROFILE%\.codex\packages\app-server-daemon\releases\0.157.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\bin\codex.exe`，PID `13884`。
- 用户已关闭自定义 NatsuTerm 命令 hooks 和 prompt-pane Stop hook，但问题仍然存在。独立的顶层 `notify` 仍指向 `codex-computer-use.exe turn-ended`。没有将这些 hook 的禁用状态当作所有运行时自动动作均已禁用的证明。
- 没有额外运行 `codex doctor`；以下来自已有进程记录与一次受控捕获。

## 复现步骤与实际结果

1. 在 Git 工作区中使用普通 Codex CLI 启动／恢复会话，连接共享 daemon。本次捕获来自已经运行的恢复会话，未声称全新配置也已复现。
2. 启动 Process Monitor，仅显示 `Process Create`；另用 `SetWinEventHook` 监听顶层窗口 SHOW／HIDE／DESTROY，在回调中读取窗口 PID、窗口类、可见状态、cloaked 状态及矩形。
3. 发送纯文字“弹窗测试 2”。该轮助手只回复文字，没有执行工具命令。
4. 发送阶段出现四个瞬时终端窗口，回复结束附近再出现一个。

预期：自动 Git 元数据查询和结束通知应在后台完成，不应弹出交互式终端窗口。

## 进程创建证据

以下时间为同一次捕获的本地时间，日期为 2026-09-26，时区 UTC+8。命令仅省略了明确列在表后面的 Git `-c` 参数。

| 创建时间 | 创建者 | 子 PID | 命令 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12:36:58.6003312 | daemon PID 13884 | 2800 | `git rev-parse HEAD` |
| 12:36:58.6096903 | daemon PID 13884 | 32064 | `git remote -v` |
| 12:36:58.6183241 | daemon PID 13884 | 33852 | `git config --null --get core.fsmonitor` |
| 12:36:59.5015174 | daemon PID 13884 | 31624 | `git status --porcelain` |
| 12:37:08.3641531 | daemon PID 13884 | 17880 | `codex-computer-use.exe turn-ended`，通知载荷已省略 |

四条 Git 命令均带 `-c safe.bareRepository=explicit`；除 `config` 查询外，其余三条还带 `-c core.hooksPath=NUL -c core.fsmonitor=false`。它们执行的是 Git 查询，不是 NatsuTerm 观察程序或 PowerShell hook。

四个 Git 进程分别创建 `Conhost.exe` PID `31992`、`33308`、`33088`、`29324`。Computer Use 辅助程序创建 `Conhost.exe` PID `2292`。

同阶段系统通过 `svchost.exe` 激活 `OpenConsole.exe -Embedding` 和 `WindowsTerminal.exe -Embedding`。不能把系统激活的 Windows Terminal 伪写成 Codex 的普通父子进程关系。

## 实际窗口证据

下表为窗口监听结果；时间由事件 tick 换算，保留到毫秒作为近似值。五次 SHOW 均实时查询到 PID，`IsWindowVisible=true`、`DWMWA_CLOAKED=0`，窗口矩形大小为 `1248 × 724`，位置在屏幕内。窗口类均为 `CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS`。Process Monitor 中相同 PID 的可执行文件均为 Windows Terminal 1.24.11911.0 的 `WindowsTerminal.exe`。

| SHOW 时间 | 窗口句柄 | 窗口所属 PID | 隐藏／销毁时间 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12:36:59.183 | `0x110368` | 32052 | 12:36:59.507 |
| 12:36:59.199 | `0xA0980` | 32052 | 12:36:59.569 |
| 12:36:59.229 | `0x409A0` | 32052 | 12:36:59.585 |
| 12:37:00.016 | `0x609B6` | 30292 | 12:37:00.258 |
| 12:37:08.873 | `0x11098A` | 33428 | 12:37:09.044 |

Git PID 32064／33852／31624 和通知进程 PID 17880 也出现 `PseudoConsoleWindow` 事件，但这些矩形为零，没有将它们计作肉眼可见的窗口。

daemon 日志同轮记录 `12:36:58 turn/start`，`12:37:08` 回复采样结束。捕获中另有桌面 App 发起的 Git，其创建时间始于 `12:37:00.0229799`，晚于上述四个发送阶段窗口的 SHOW 时间。

## 对照及证据边界

- 重启 Windows 后普通模式仍出现弹窗。
- 同版本使用 `codex.cmd --no-daemon` 新建对话，单轮纯文字交互没有弹窗。尚未用该模式验证全部工具调用或 Computer Use 功能。
- 已直接对应实际窗口句柄、宿主 PID 和可执行文件。Git／通知子进程与这些窗口的时间、数量和控制台活动一致，但没有逐个证明前三个窗口分别绑定哪个 Git PID。
- 尚未捕获对应启动调用的 `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` 等标志，也未对当前二进制定位到具体源码行；不把相关 issue 中的源码分析当成本机已验证结论。
- 原始通知命令可能包含会话内容，因此只发布上述脱敏摘要，不附完整命令行、环境或原始捕获文件。

items.title: `codex plugin list` shows opaque `app-<id>` names for many openai-curated-remote plugins

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

`codex plugin list` shows many plugins from the `openai-curated-remote` marketplace using opaque internal IDs such as:

```text
app-6a057d268ebc81919918d37eec718425@openai-curated-remote
app-69ea4ed2cf7c8191b742ef3622479ddd@openai-curated-remote
app-6a314a73f8ac819195b0d55e36b9c609@openai-curated-remote
app-6a502589384081919c5decf93496c9d1@openai-curated-remote
app-69bc11db874881918718abaca20b68ce@openai-curated-remote
```

These are real named plugins/apps. For example, the corresponding public plugin pages identify some of these as Remote Desktop Commander, Exa, Firecrawl, Railway, and Interactive Brokers.

Other entries in the same marketplace render correctly with human-readable names, e.g.:

```text
github@openai-curated-remote
google-drive@openai-curated-remote
slack@openai-curated-remote
notion@openai-curated-remote
supabase@openai-curated-remote
```

This makes the CLI output difficult to browse and makes it look like the remote catalog contains unnamed or malformed plugins when the display names actually exist.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign into Codex with an account that has access to the remote plugin catalog.
2. Run:

```bash
codex plugin list
```

3. Inspect the `Marketplace 'openai-curated-remote'` section.
4. Observe that many entries are rendered as `app-<opaque-id>@openai-curated-remote` instead of their public plugin names.

Example output:

```text
PLUGIN                                                            STATUS
gmail@openai-curated-remote                                       not installed
google-drive@openai-curated-remote                                installed, enabled
github@openai-curated-remote                                      installed, enabled
app-6a057d268ebc81919918d37eec718425@openai-curated-remote        not installed
canva@openai-curated-remote                                       not installed
supabase@openai-curated-remote                                    not installed
app-69ea4ed2cf7c8191b742ef3622479ddd@openai-curated-remote        not installed
slack@openai-curated-remote                                       installed, enabled
```

### Expected behavior

`codex plugin list` should use the plugin's human-readable/canonical name when that metadata is available.

For example, an entry corresponding to Firecrawl should render something like:

```text
firecrawl@openai-curated-remote
```

rather than:

```text
app-6a314a73f8ac819195b0d55e36b9c609@openai-curated-remote
```

If the canonical slug and display name are distinct, the CLI could show both, but it should not fall back to an opaque internal app ID when public naming metadata exists.

### Additional information

- Platform: Linux
- The issue affects the remote catalog listing itself; the affected entries do not need to be installed.
- The same catalog contains correctly named and opaque entries side-by-side.
- The source field for the opaque entries is also an internal App SDK identifier such as `plugin_asdk_app_6a314a73f8ac819195b0d55e36b9c609`, suggesting the CLI may be falling back to an internal ID rather than resolving the catalog display/canonical name.
- I searched existing Codex issues for `openai-curated-remote`, `codex plugin list`, `displayName`, and `app-` and found related catalog/plugin issues, but not one specifically covering this naming behavior.

It would also be useful for the CLI and Desktop plugin directory to use the same canonical naming metadata so the same plugin has a consistent identity across surfaces.

items.title: [Linux][Desktop] Local tasks hang on “Starting your task”; Desktop never sends turn/start while CLI works

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
## Environment

- **OS:** Arch Linux x86_64
- **Desktop:** GNOME / Wayland
- **Current OpenAI package:** `chatgpt-bin 26.924.20706-1`, installed from the official OpenAI Arch package repository
- **Desktop client version:** `26.924.20706`
- **Bundled Codex CLI:** `0.158.0-alpha.2`
- **Authentication mode:** ChatGPT
- **Current API-key environment overrides:** none detected

## Issue

Codex Desktop local conversations are unusable. Sending even a trivial message in a brand-new local conversation leaves the UI indefinitely at:

> Starting your task

Existing local conversations also hang.

The important diagnostic boundary is that, during a fresh failed Desktop task, the app-server remains responsive and receives authentication/status and thread requests, but the Desktop client never sends a `turn/start` request.

The same installed Codex runtime on the same machine and account works from the command line and successfully receives a model response.

This persisted across package replacement and multiple clean-state tests.

## Timeline

### Before failure

At **2026-09-25 15:58:47 local time (PDT)**, the then-running Desktop client was functioning normally.

Logs show:

```text
app_server.client_name="Codex Desktop"
app_server.client_version="26.915.31945"

app-server request: getAuthStatus
app-server request: turn/start
app-server event: turn/started
auth_mode=Chatgpt
```

The turn then received normal model output. Additional `turn/start` requests were successfully dispatched afterward.

### 401 failure

Beginning shortly afterward, requests to `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` began returning:

```text
401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided:
sk-svcac*******************************************************************fvMA
```

The client was using:

```text
auth_mode="Chatgpt"
auth_header_attached=true
auth_env_openai_api_key_present=false
auth_env_codex_api_key_present=false
auth_env_codex_api_key_enabled=false
auth_env_provider_key_present=false
```

The logs show managed auth recovery being attempted. Credential refresh succeeded at the OAuth endpoint, but the retry to `/responses` still returned 401.

This coincided with the Sep 25 Codex authentication incident. Other reports from the same date show the same redacted `sk-svcac...fvMA` credential pattern (for example #48247).

### Persistent failure after service recovery

After the service recovered, Desktop did not recover locally.

The installation was eventually changed to the current official OpenAI Arch package:

```text
chatgpt-bin 26.924.20706-1
```

The symptom remained unchanged.

Importantly, the failure **began before** these package changes.

## Current reproduction

1. Start ChatGPT/Codex Desktop normally.
2. Create a brand-new local conversation/task.
3. Enter a trivial prompt.
4. Send it.
5. UI displays **“Starting your task”** indefinitely.

This also occurs with existing local conversations.

## App-server observation during reproduction

A captured log window from a fresh failed task contains repeated requests such as:

```text
app-server request: getAuthStatus
app-server request: getAuthStatus
...
app-server request: thread/read
...
```

The app-server continues servicing requests.

However, in the captured failed-task trace:

```text
turn/start occurrences: 0
```

No `turn/start` reaches the app-server while the UI claims it is “Starting your task.”

This differs from the pre-failure trace, where `turn/start` and `turn/started` are plainly present.

## CLI control test

The bundled/current Codex CLI was invoked directly on the same machine using the existing authentication:

```text
OpenAI Codex v0.158.0-alpha.2
workdir: /tmp
model: gpt-6-luna
provider: openai
approval: never
sandbox: read-only
reasoning effort: medium

user
Reply with exactly: AUTH_OK

codex
AUTH_OK
```

Therefore the same machine/account can:

- start a new Codex session;
- authenticate;
- reach OpenAI;
- submit a model request; and
- receive a valid response.

The failure appears specific to the Desktop task-dispatch path before `turn/start`.

## Local state checks

SQLite integrity checks were run against the primary local stores:

```text
thread_history_1.sqlite: ok
state_5.sqlite: ok
logs_2.sqlite: ok
```

A fresh local Desktop task fails too, so the problem is not limited to one historical conversation.

Current model-list requests report:

```text
auth_header_attached=true
auth_mode="Chatgpt"
auth_error=""
auth_error_code=""
auth_env_openai_api_key_present=false
auth_env_codex_api_key_present=false
auth_env_codex_api_key_enabled=false
auth_env_provider_key_present=false
```

## Isolation already performed

All tests below preserved conversation/session data.

1. **Reinstalled/replaced Desktop package**
   - Failure began before package changes.
   - Persisted through an updated repack and then the official OpenAI Arch package.

2. **Desktop cache reset**
   - Moved `~/.cache/Codex` aside and allowed it to regenerate.
   - No change.

3. **Fresh Electron/Chromium profile**
   - Launched Desktop with a temporary clean `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`.
   - No change.

4. **Fresh Codex global UI state**
   - Preserved and temporarily removed:
     - `~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json`
     - `~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json.bak`
   - Allowed Desktop to generate fresh state.
   - No change.
   - Original state was restored afterward.

5. **Environment API-key check**
   - No OpenAI/Codex API-key/token environment override was present.

6. **Bundled CLI control**
   - Succeeds with `AUTH_OK`.

No conversation databases or session/rollout data were deleted.

## Expected behavior

Submitting a prompt to a new local Desktop conversation should cause Desktop to dispatch the task to the app-server (`turn/start`) and begin the local Codex turn.

## Actual behavior

Desktop displays **“Starting your task”** indefinitely, while the app-server remains responsive but never receives `turn/start`.

## Why this may be distinct from existing “Starting your task” reports

There are existing reports such as #42794 where “Starting your task” is associated with thread-history projection failures.

This reproduction has a different observed boundary:

- SQLite integrity checks pass.
- A completely new local task also fails.
- The failed-task trace contains no `turn/start`.
- The CLI works with the same machine/account.
- Resetting Desktop cache, the Electron profile, and Codex global UI state does not change the symptom.

That suggests the failure occurs in Desktop before task dispatch rather than during model execution or durable rollout projection.

## Potentially relevant upstream event

The first observed failure followed the Sep 25, 2026 Codex 401 incident.

During that event this machine received the same unusual:

```text
Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...fvMA
```

error reported by other Codex Desktop users.

I do **not** know whether the 401 incident caused the persistent Desktop state. The timing is included because it is the clearest onset boundary available.

## Diagnostic artifacts available

I can provide sanitized extracts containing:

- the working pre-failure `turn/start` / `turn/started` sequence;
- the 401 retry/recovery sequence;
- the post-recovery Desktop trace showing repeated `getAuthStatus` / `thread/read` but no `turn/start`;
- SQLite schema/integrity results; and
- the successful CLI control-test output.

Full raw logs may contain account identifiers, request IDs, paths, or authentication-adjacent metadata, so I would prefer to provide a minimized sanitized trace if requested.

---

### Minimal evidence

**Working Desktop before onset**
```text
15:58:47  getAuthStatus
15:58:47  turn/start
15:58:48  turn/started
15:58:48  auth_mode=Chatgpt
15:58:54  model output received
```

**During 401 incident**
```text
POST /backend-api/codex/responses
→ 401 Incorrect API key ... sk-svcac...fvMA

auth_mode=Chatgpt
managed auth recovery attempted
credential refresh/retry performed
follow-up /responses request → 401
```

**Current broken Desktop**
```text
getAuthStatus
getAuthStatus
...
thread/read
...
[no turn/start]
```

**Current working CLI**
```text
Codex 0.158.0-alpha.2
provider: openai
sandbox: read-only

Reply with exactly: AUTH_OK
→ AUTH_OK
```

**Suspected boundary**
```text
Desktop renderer / Desktop task-start state
        |
        | repeated auth/status activity
        |
        X  turn/start never dispatched
        |
Codex app-server / runtime
        |
        +-- independently verified working through CLI
```
